assumptions.condition: The coordinates \(N_j\), \(j\in I\), are mutually independent.
Each \(f_j\) is continuous on its compact parent domain and three times continuously differentiable on its relative interior.

standard.name: three-times differentiable nonlinear ANM mechanism condition

assumptions.condition: Each \(p_{N_j}\) is three times continuously differentiable and strictly positive on the relative interior of its compact interval support.

novel.justification: This is a compact-support adaptation of the positive-density regime used by Peters et al., not their published premise. Smooth compact bump innovations satisfy it and model measurements with hard feasibility limits while allowing exact density decay only at the boundary.
Bounded physical measurements and bounded innovations satisfy this compatibility condition after choosing the recorded node ranges to contain every feasible structural output.

assumptions.condition: For every edge \(u\to v\) of \(G_0\), the map \(x_u\mapsto f_v(x_u,x_{\operatorname{pa}_0(v)\setminus\{u\}})\) is nonconstant on a set of positive parent-law measure.

novel.justification: This strengthens the pointwise nonconstancy characterization in Peters et al., Proposition 17, for the compact-support setting. Requiring each parent effect to be nonconstant on a set of positive parent-law measure ensures, under the relative-interior density and smoothness conditions, that the effect is nonconstant on a positive-law interior set rather than only at boundary or null configurations, which is the form needed by the compact identification bridge.

assumptions.condition: For every \(v\in I\), every \(u\in\operatorname{pa}_0(v)\), and every \(A\) satisfying \(\operatorname{pa}_0(v)\setminus\{u\}\subseteq A\subseteq\operatorname{nd}_0(v)\setminus\{u,v\}\), there is an interior \(x_A\) of positive density such that the section \(x_u\mapsto f_v(x_{\operatorname{pa}_0(v)\setminus\{u\}},x_u)\), the conditional law \(\mathcal L(V_u\mid V_A=x_A)\), and \(\mathcal L(N_v)\) satisfy Peters et al.'s Condition 19 by failing their differential equation (7) on some open part of its domain.

novel.justification: This is the compact-section analogue of Peters et al.'s Condition 19 configuration requirement. It is directly checkable for smooth compact mechanisms and bump innovations by evaluating their differential equation on an interior section; failure on an open section is stable under small three-times continuously differentiable perturbations and includes the quadratic and cosine mechanisms used here.

assumptions.condition: Every nonempty conditional support fiber appearing in Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\) has connected relative interior.

novel.justification: Convex innovation supports combined with monotone triangular mechanisms give connected interval fibers, covering compact measurement systems while excluding disconnected-support reversals.

assumptions.condition: There is a constant \(\underline v>0\) such that \(\min_{j\in I}\operatorname{Var}_P(V_j)\ge\underline v\).
Every weakly connected component of \(G_0\) is either an isolated vertex or one directed edge.

novel.justification: Independent cause--effect modules arise in separately engineered subsystems and controlled benchmark suites; this graph regime isolates a directly checkable mechanism-level certificate.

The inequality is an integral condition computed from a structural function, a root density, and an innovation density; small-noise monotone mechanisms and symmetric many-to-one mechanisms satisfy it without comparing permutation scores.

assumptions.condition: The observations \(V^{(1)},\ldots,V^{(n)}\) are independent draws from \(P\).
For every \(v\in I\) and \(A\subseteq I\setminus\{v\}\), \(\mu_{v,A}\) belongs to a radius-bounded Holder ball of smoothness three on \(\mathcal X_A\).
For each \(A\subseteq I\), the density of \(P_A\) is bounded above and bounded away from zero on the relative interior of its support.
constants: the upper and lower density bounds

standard.name: regular random-design density condition for Holder regression

assumptions.condition: Every kernel in \(k\) is bounded, continuous, and characteristic.

There is \(L_k<\infty\) such that every residual-coordinate factor satisfies \(|k^{\varepsilon}_{v,A}(e,e')-k^{\varepsilon}_{v,A}(\tilde e,\tilde e')|\le L_k(|e-\tilde e|+|e'-\tilde e'|)\) on the compact residual range.

novel.justification: This explicitly nonstandard perturbation premise is satisfied by Gaussian and Laplace residual kernels restricted to compact residual ranges, covering the usual smooth kernels used for residual-independence screening.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_0(d)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_0(d)=\{(G_0,f,p_N,P):j\in\{1,\ldots,d\},\ V_j=f_j(V_{\operatorname{pa}_0(j)})+N_j,\ P=\mathcal L(V),\text{ and the eight member properties below hold}\}\).

definitions.name: conditional mean and risk
definitions.construction: \(\mu_{v,A}(x_A)=\mathbb E_P[V_v\mid V_A=x_A]\) and \(R_{v,A}=\inf_{g\in L^2(P_A)}\mathbb E_P[(V_v-g(V_A))^2]=\mathbb E_P[(V_v-\mu_{v,A}(V_A))^2]\), with \(R_{v,\varnothing}=\operatorname{Var}_P(V_v)\).

definitions.name: insertion and score gain
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Ins}_{r\to s}(\pi)\) removes the node at rank \(r\), shifts the traversed block by one rank, and reinserts that node at rank \(s\); \(C_P(\pi;r,s)=S_P(\operatorname{Ins}_{r\to s}(\pi))-S_P(\pi)\) for \(r\ne s\).

definitions.name: ancestral reversal potential and correcting moves
primitive edge signal ratios
definitions.construction: For an edge \(u\to v\) that is a weak component, set \(p_u(x)=p_{N_u}(x-f_u)\), \(p_v(y)=\int p_u(x)p_{N_v}(y-f_v(x))\,dx\), and \(m_{uv}(y)=\int xp_u(x)p_{N_v}(y-f_v(x))\,dx/p_v(y)\). Define \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}=\operatorname{Var}_{p_u}(f_v(X_u))/[\operatorname{Var}_{p_u}(f_v(X_u))+\operatorname{Var}(N_v)]\) and \(\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}=\operatorname{Var}_{p_v}(m_{uv}(V_v))/\operatorname{Var}_{p_u}(X_u)\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)=\{(G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_0(d):\text{ every weak component is an isolated vertex or one edge and }\rho^{\to}_{uv}>(d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\text{ for every }u\to v\}\).

definitions.name: primitive pairwise slack
definitions.construction: \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}=\min_{u\to v\text{ in }G_0}\{\rho^{\to}_{uv}-(d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\}\), with \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}=1\) if the edge set is empty.

definitions.name: oracle GENE recovery map
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{or}}(P,\pi)\) repeatedly applies an insertion attaining \(\max_{r\ne s}C_P(\pi;r,s)>0\) until no positive gain remains; from the resulting complete ordered DAG it repeatedly deletes \(u\to v\) exactly when \(H(v,A\setminus\{u\},u)=0\), with \(A\) the current ordered parent set of \(v\).

definitions.name: quadratic small-noise witness
definitions.construction: Under \(P_{\mathrm w,\sigma}\), \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(Y=X+X^2+\sigma Z\), and \(Z\) has mean zero and density proportional to \(\exp\{-1/(1-z^2)\}\mathbf 1\{|z|<1\}\); take the node interval for \(Y\) to be \([-\sigma,2+\sigma]\).

definitions.name: six-node strict-comparison witness
definitions.construction: Let \(G_0\) have edges \(1\to2\), \(3\to4\), and \(5\to6\). Let \(V_1,V_3,V_5\) be independent with density \(g(x)\propto\exp\{-1/[x(1-x)]\}\mathbf 1\{0<x<1\}\), let \(Z_2,Z_4,Z_6\) be independent with density \(b(z)\propto\exp\{-1/(1-z^2)\}\mathbf 1\{|z|<1\}\), and set \(V_2=\cos(2\pi V_1)+\sigma Z_2\), \(V_4=V_3+V_3^2+\sigma Z_4\), and \(V_6=V_5+V_5^2+\sigma Z_6\). Use node intervals \([0,1]\), \([-1-\sigma,1+\sigma]\), \([0,1]\), \([-\sigma,2+\sigma]\), \([0,1]\), and \([-\sigma,2+\sigma]\), and denote the induced law by \(P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}\).

definitions.name: rare-component smoothing handle
definitions.construction: Start from a rare two-component root passed through a separated additive location channel; express \(q(X,\{Y\})\) by posterior classification risk and \(q(Y,\{X\})\) by between-component variance, then replace both root components and the noise by interior-positive compact bump densities and control the two risks and reverse-residual HSIC uniformly in the smoothing radius.

definitions.name: cross-fitted bands and separated-model decisions
definitions.construction: Split \(\mathcal Z_n\) into regression and evaluation folds, estimate every \(\mu_{v,A}\) off-fold, and evaluate squared loss and bounded-kernel HSIC on held-out folds to form simultaneous intervals \(\mathcal B^R_{v,A}\) and \(\mathcal B^H_{v,A,u}\). Intersect each HSIC interval with \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), recording \(\mathrm{ind}\) when the intersection contains \(0\), \(\mathrm{dep}\) when it meets \([\lambda,\infty)\), both when both are possible, and both when the intersection is empty. Propagate the risk intervals and these decisions through every insertion gain and pruning step; let \(w_S\) be the largest resulting gain half-width and let \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\) be the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, with all labelled DAGs returned if that union is empty.

statements.statement: Every law in \(\mathcal M_0(d)\) identifies \(G_0\). Support closure first makes the structural recursion a law on \(\mathcal X\). On every nonempty conditional-support fiber, the induced density is positive and three times continuously differentiable on a connected relative interior. The conditional-independence intersection argument therefore applies on that open set, connectedness rules out patching distinct reverse factorizations across disjoint interior components, and the support boundary is null. Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\) then supplies an interior open set on which Peters et al.'s differential identity fails, excluding every reversed bivariate conditional ANM. These steps extend their positive-density Condition 19 argument to the stated compact-support regime without assuming uniqueness of the DAG.
statements.justification: The compact-domain model needs a genuine identification bridge because positivity only on relative interiors is weaker than full-support positivity.
statements.gap: Peters et al. (2014, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28) do not state the support-closed compact-fiber extension.
statements.consumer: The score analysis can target the labelled DAG using a proved compact restricted-ANM identification result.

statements.statement: Let \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\). For every \(\pi\notin\Pi(G_0)\), choose a component edge \(u\to v\) with \(v\) before \(u\) and insert \(u\) immediately before \(v\). This move belongs to \(\operatorname{Corr}_{G_0}(\pi)\) and satisfies \(C_P(\pi;r,s)\ge\rho^{\to}_{uv}-(d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\ge\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}>0\). The bound follows from the structural product law: before the move the reversed root contributes at most \((d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\), after the move the effect contributes \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}\), and every traversed node from another independent component has unchanged explained risk and a weakly larger GENE penalty factor. Consequently every insertion-local maximizer is topological.
statements.justification: This is the field-level root result: a check on mechanisms and noise laws yields strict local ascent without assuming any ordering of permutation scores.
statements.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3) assume a global ranking for every pair of orders with different ancestral-reversal counts and give no structural-function condition implying a correcting insertion.
statements.consumer: Benchmark designers can certify population success of insertion search directly from each cause--effect module.

statements.statement: Li et al.'s global reversal-monotone premise implies the positive correcting-move property on the matching-component graph class, but the converse fails even for smooth identifiable ANMs. For all sufficiently small \(\sigma>0\), \(P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(6)\): symmetry gives \(\rho^{\leftarrow}_{12}=0\), while \(\rho^{\to}_{12}\to1\) and both directional ratios on edges \(3\to4\) and \(5\to6\) converge to \(1\). Nevertheless, for \(\pi_1=(2,3,4,5,6,1)\) and \(\pi_2=(1,2,4,6,3,5)\), \(\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_1)=1<2=\operatorname{Rev}_{G_0}(\pi_2)\), whereas \(S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_1)\to2\) and \(S_{P_{\mathrm{sep},\sigma}}(\pi_2)\to1+4/5+5/6>2\). Continuity of the correlation ratios, together with forward residual independence and Condition 19 reverse dependence for every \(\sigma>0\), makes the reversed ranking strict for small positive \(\sigma\). Thus Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) guarantees local recovery for a support-closed smooth law excluded by Li et al.'s premise.
statements.justification: An explicit score-limit calculation certifies a strict reduction in the recovery hypothesis, rather than a verbal comparison between differently named conditions.
statements.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3 and its proof on page 5) establish sufficiency of global reversal monotonicity but do not separate it from the local property their optimizer needs.
statements.consumer: Users obtain a guarantee for heterogeneous modular systems whose inversion costs cannot be ranked by an unweighted reversal count.

statements.statement: For \(P_{\mathrm w,\sigma}\), the forward residual is independent of \(X\), the reverse conditional-mean residual is dependent on \(Y\), and, with \(m_2=\mathbb E[Z^2]\), \(C_{P_{\mathrm w,\sigma}}((Y,X);2,1)\ge1/2-\sigma^2m_2/\operatorname{Var}(X+X^2)\). Hence the correcting gain is positive for sufficiently small \(\sigma\) and converges to \(1/2\). The support-closure relation holds on \([0,1]\times[-\sigma,2+\sigma]\), and the Condition 19 differential identity fails on an interior open set.
statements.justification: The witness supplies a quantitative, scale-invariant calibration of the primitive certificate in the smallest graph.
statements.gap: Reisach et al. (2023, Sections 3 and 5) analyze normalized explained variance but not its combination with exact residual dependence in GENE Equation (6).
statements.consumer: Implementers obtain an analytic two-node test case whose population gain approaches one half.

statements.statement: If \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), then \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{or}}(P,\pi)=G_0\) for every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_I\). Strict ascent prevents revisiting an order, and Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) makes every terminal order topological; Condition 19 configurations and causal minimality then make residual-independence pruning delete exactly the nonedges. The search uses at most \(d!-1\) insertions and \(d(d-1)d!\) gain comparisons. Memoization uses at most \(d2^{d-1}\) conditional-risk queries and \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC queries, followed by at most \(d(d-1)/2\) pruning checks.
statements.justification: The primitive certificate is useful only if it yields a complete labelled-DAG recovery theorem and a finite oracle budget.
statements.gap: Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Proposition 8 and Theorem 9) study covered-arrow walks for sparsity, while Li et al. (2025) do not give primitive risk and dependence query counts for GENE.
statements.consumer: An implementation can cache the finite local-score table and know its worst-case population-query budget.

statements.statement: Does there exist an explicitly parameterized relatively open subset of \(\mathcal M_0(2)\) and \(\eta>0\) such that every law in the subset satisfies \(q(X,\{Y\})/2-q(Y,\{X\})\ge\eta\) and \(H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0\)? Equivalently, can the rare-component smoothing handle produce an interior-positive support-closed identifiable ANM for which the wrong order \((Y,X)\) is a strict insertion-local maximizer of the exact \(\alpha=1\) score?
statements.justification: A strict open trap would distinguish failure of this hybrid optimization score from failure of causal identification.
statements.gap: Neither Li et al. (2025) nor Reisach et al. (2023) construct a robust smooth wrong-order local maximum for GENE Equation (6).
statements.consumer: Method developers obtain a concrete stress-test family for deciding whether a different neighborhood or score is required.

statements.statement: Under Assumptions \(\ref{ass:iid-sampling}\), \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\), \(\ref{ass:design-density}\), \(\ref{ass:characteristic-kernels}\), and \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\), there is \(K<\infty\) such that, with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), all \(d2^{d-1}\) risks and all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant residual-HSIC values lie in their cross-fitted bands, with \(w_R\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n^2\}\) and \(w_H\le K\{\sqrt{\log(M_d/\alpha)/n}+a_n\}\). Boundedness of the kernels controls the held-out empirical fluctuation in \(w_H\), while Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\) is used only to convert the cross-fitted residual error into the additive \(a_n\) term. On this event, if \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\), every queried HSIC value belongs to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and \(2w_H<\lambda\), then \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\). Without the two separation inequalities, interval propagation retains every compatible decision and reports more than one graph whenever the data do not separate zero from the positive-HSIC region.
statements.justification: The finite-sample theorem ties singleton recovery to the primitive gain slack and an explicit pruning resolution while preserving abstention near the discontinuity at independence.
statements.gap: Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) and Shekhar et al. (2023, Theorems 6 and 7) do not jointly cover learned normalized risks, simultaneous residual perturbations, adaptive insertions, and separated-model graph confidence sets.
statements.consumer: Users receive a certified labelled DAG only when both navigation and pruning margins dominate propagated uncertainty.

sampling_model.design: Observational independent sampling from one support-closed compact restricted additive-noise law \(P\).
sampling_model.units: The units \(V^{(1)},\ldots,V^{(n)}\) are independent draws of all \(d\) labelled nodes.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the labelled DAG \(G_0\).
sampling_model.overlap: Innovation densities are strictly positive on relative interiors, conditional-support fibers are connected, feasible structural outputs stay inside the declared node intervals, and node variances are bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted local-polynomial regression estimates conditional means; held-out squared losses estimate risks, bounded continuous characteristic kernels estimate residual HSIC, and a separate residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise controls plug-in residual perturbations.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.3 assumes that any two orders with different ancestral-reversal counts are strictly fitness-ranked in the opposite direction and concludes that greedy search terminates at a true order.
The terminal-node normalized explained variance in a random linear causal chain converges to one under a positive mean log-edge-weight condition.
A causally minimal restricted additive-noise model satisfying the Condition 19 configuration requirement has a DAG identifiable from its observational distribution.
Greedy sparsest-permutation algorithms are pointwise consistent under faithfulness through weakly decreasing covered-arrow walks.
Sample splitting gives a fitted-residual dHSIC statistic the same asymptotic null distribution as its exact-residual counterpart.
Studentized cross-HSIC converges to a standard normal law under fixed bounded-kernel null distributions satisfying a second-moment condition.
A likelihood order estimator is consistent when the minimum wrong-order log-residual-variance gap is positive.

tldr: On support-closed compact restricted additive-noise models whose graph is a matching, the primitive edgewise inequality \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}>(d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\) forces every non-topological order to have a strictly improving reversal-correcting insertion. It follows directly that best-improvement GENE search and residual-independence pruning recover the labelled DAG with a finite oracle-query budget. A six-node smooth witness satisfies this local structural certificate while violating Li et al.'s global reversal-monotone premise through explicit score limits. Cross-fitted simultaneous risk and HSIC bands yield singleton recovery only when the primitive gain slack and a pruning separation margin dominate propagated uncertainty, and otherwise return a compatible graph set. A smooth open family with a trapped wrong order remains the first-class converse question.

project_justification.gap: Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3) impose a global score ranking over all pairs of orders with different ancestral-reversal counts. Peters et al. (2014) identify restricted ANMs through Condition 19 configurations, but this observational identification gives no local ascent property for GENE's hybrid score.
project_justification.niche: The missing theorem is a directly checkable condition on structural functions and noise laws that guarantees a correcting insertion, together with evidence that it covers identifiable laws excluded by global reversal monotonicity.
project_justification.fill: The pairwise forward-versus-reverse signal inequality yields a strict gain lower bound on support-closed matching-component ANMs. A six-node cosine--quadratic law proves strict separation from Li et al., and the resulting navigation theorem drives oracle recovery, query complexity, a calibrated positive witness, and margin-aware set-valued inference.

related_work: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6), Definition 4.1, and Theorem 4.3 with its proof on page 5) define the score and insertion search and assume global reversal monotonicity; Theorem 3 proves a strict reduction of that premise on a smooth six-node ANM. Peters et al. (2014, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28 on pages 13--16) prove identification under their positive-density restricted-ANM configuration requirement. Their Proposition 17 supplies only the pointwise nonconstancy characterization of causal minimality; the positive-parent-law-measure formulation used here is a strengthened compact-support premise. They do not state the present compact-support, relative-interior version; Lemma 1 supplies support closure, connected conditional-support fibers, localization of the differential obstruction to a positive-density interior open set, and the null-boundary step. Reisach et al. (2023, Sections 3 and 5) show how normalized explained variance responds to mechanism and noise strength, informing the primitive ratios without supplying the GENE landscape theorem. Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Proposition 8 and Theorem 9) analyze covered-arrow moves for a sparsity score, not insertion ascent for the GENE score. Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) support bounded continuous characteristic kernels and fitted-residual sample splitting, but the residual-coordinate Lipschitz perturbation premise used for the \(a_n\) term in \(w_H\) is separate and explicitly nonstandard. Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (2023, Theorems 6 and 7) derive cross-HSIC null limits but not adaptive GENE graph sets. Buhlmann, Peters, and Ernest (2014, Theorems 1 and 2) separate likelihood order estimation from pruning under a wrong-order variance gap, a different score and margin.
technical_internal_limitation: The structural certificate is sufficient and applies to matching-component DAGs; it does not characterize general GENE landscapes. Exact independence is discontinuous, so finite-sample singleton recovery is stated only on the separated HSIC parameter space and under a propagated score-radius inequality. The \(a_n\) residual-estimation contribution to the HSIC band uses an explicitly nonstandard residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise. The rare-component construction remains an open question until smoothing is shown to preserve both its strict risk inequality and nonzero reverse-residual HSIC.
honest_scope: The compact-support identification lemma, direct pairwise navigation theorem, six-node strict comparison, oracle recovery theorem, quadratic positive witness, and simultaneous-band theorem are proof targets. The structural result is sufficient on matching-component DAGs. The smooth trapped family is an open-ended construction problem. When \(d=2\), the navigation bound reduces to \(C_P((Y,X);2,1)\ge\rho^{\to}_{XY}-\rho^{\leftarrow}_{XY}/2>0\), the familiar forward-versus-reverse residual comparison for this exact score. The released Sachs workflow is only an audit case: a fixed chi-square threshold cannot certify a population margin, and intervention-informed reference orientations are not consequences of an observational acyclic ANM alone.

novelty_justification: The root claim is a non-definitional implication from the structural product law and the primitive inequality \(\rho^{\to}_{uv}>(d-1)\rho^{\leftarrow}_{uv}/d\) to a positive correcting insertion. The six-node cosine--quadratic witness satisfies the primitive condition while reversing the score ordering required by Li et al. (2025, Theorem 4.3), with limits \(2\) and \(1+4/5+5/6\) for explicit orders. Peters et al.'s published positive-density Condition 19 identification result motivates, but is distinct from, the compact-support adaptations used here: relative-interior positive innovation densities, interior-section Condition 19 configurations, and positive-parent-law-measure nonconstancy. Peters et al.'s Proposition 17 supplies only the pointwise nonconstancy characterization; the strengthened formulation ensures that the relevant parent effect is nonconstant on a positive-law interior set for the compact identification bridge. Support closure, connected relative-interior fibers, local positivity, and null boundaries complete that bridge. The HSIC theorem separately distinguishes Pfister-supported bounded continuous characteristic kernels from the nonstandard residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise used only for its \(a_n\) perturbation term. This yields a field-level sufficient theorem, a theorem-level strict comparator separation, and inference tied to primitive gain and pruning margins.
